nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u, v$ be words over $A$, and write $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ for the context quotient. If the image of the syntactic morphism of $L$ and the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$ are both finite, then the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$ has at most as many elements as the image of the syntactic morphism of $L$.
nodes.title: Size bound for the syntactic monoid of a context quotient

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$, let $P \subseteq M$, and let $u, v$ be words over $A$. The accepting set for the context $(u, v)$ is $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m\, \varphi(v) \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Accepting set for a context quotient

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$ that recognizes a language $L$ over $A$ through $P \subseteq M$, that is, a word $x$ lies in $L$ exactly when $\varphi(x) \in P$. Then for all words $u, v$ over $A$, $\varphi$ recognizes the context quotient $\{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ through the set $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m\, \varphi(v) \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Recognizers recognize context quotients

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $A$, then for all words $u, v$ over $A$, the context quotient $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ is regular.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under context quotients

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, and for words $u, v$ over $A$ write $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$. Then for all words $u_1, v_1, u_2, v_2$ over $A$, $u_2^{-1} (u_1^{-1} L v_1^{-1}) v_2^{-1} = (u_1 u_2)^{-1} L (v_2 v_1)^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Composing context quotients

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u, v$ be words over $A$, and write $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$. Let $\eta$ be the syntactic morphism of $L$ and $\eta'$ the syntactic morphism of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$. This is the monoid morphism from the image of $\eta$ to the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L v^{-1}$ that sends $\eta(x)$ to $\eta'(x)$ for every word $x$ over $A$.
nodes.title: The canonical map to the syntactic monoid of a context quotient

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ and let $u, v$ be words over $A$. The context quotient of $L$ by $(u, v)$ is the language $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \in A^* \mid uxv \in L\}$ of words that land in $L$ when placed between $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Context quotient

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then for all words $u, v$ over $A$, the syntactic monoid of the context quotient $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{x \mid uxv \in L\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Context quotients preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, the syntactic monoid of the left quotient $u^{-1} L = \{x \mid ux \in L\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Left quotients preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$ whose syntactic monoid is finite. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, the syntactic monoid of the right quotient $L u^{-1} = \{x \mid xu \in L\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Right quotients preserve finiteness of the syntactic monoid

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $A$, then for every word $u$ over $A$, the left quotient $u^{-1} L = \{x \mid ux \in L\}$ is regular.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under left quotients by fixed words

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$, let $P \subseteq M$, and let $u$ be a word over $A$. The accepting set for the left quotient by $u$ is $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Accepting set for a left quotient

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u$ be a word over $A$, and write $u^{-1} L = \{x \mid ux \in L\}$. Let $\eta$ be the syntactic morphism of $L$ and $\eta'$ the syntactic morphism of $u^{-1} L$. This is the monoid morphism from the image of $\eta$ to the syntactic monoid of $u^{-1} L$ that sends $\eta(x)$ to $\eta'(x)$ for every word $x$ over $A$.
nodes.title: The canonical map to the syntactic monoid of a left quotient

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$ that recognizes a language $L$ over $A$ through $P \subseteq M$, that is, a word $x$ lies in $L$ exactly when $\varphi(x) \in P$. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, $\varphi$ recognizes the left quotient $\{x \mid ux \in L\}$ through the set $\{m \in M \mid \varphi(u)\, m \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Recognizers recognize left quotients

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$ that recognizes a language $L$ over $A$ through $P \subseteq M$, that is, a word $x$ lies in $L$ exactly when $\varphi(x) \in P$. Then for every word $u$ over $A$, $\varphi$ recognizes the right quotient $\{x \mid xu \in L\}$ through the set $\{m \in M \mid m\, \varphi(u) \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Recognizers recognize right quotients

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a regular language over an alphabet $A$, then for every word $u$ over $A$, the right quotient $L u^{-1} = \{x \mid xu \in L\}$ is regular.
nodes.title: Regular languages are closed under right quotients by fixed words

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi \colon A^* \to M$ be a monoid morphism from the free monoid on an alphabet $A$ to a monoid $M$, let $P \subseteq M$, and let $u$ be a word over $A$. The accepting set for the right quotient by $u$ is $\{m \in M \mid m\, \varphi(u) \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Accepting set for a right quotient

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$, let $u$ be a word over $A$, and write $L u^{-1} = \{x \mid xu \in L\}$. Let $\eta$ be the syntactic morphism of $L$ and $\eta'$ the syntactic morphism of $L u^{-1}$. This is the monoid morphism from the image of $\eta$ to the syntactic monoid of $L u^{-1}$ that sends $\eta(x)$ to $\eta'(x)$ for every word $x$ over $A$.
nodes.title: The canonical map to the syntactic monoid of a right quotient

nodes.summary: For a language $L$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$ and a word $w \in \Sigma^*$, the right quotient of $L$ by $w$ is the language $\{x \in \Sigma^* : xw \in L\}$ of all words $x$ whose concatenation $xw$ with $w$ lies in $L$.
nodes.title: Right quotient of a language by a word

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $A$. Two words $x, y$ over $A$ are syntactically equivalent for $L$ if and only if, for all words $u, v$ over $A$, $x$ lies in the context quotient $u^{-1} L v^{-1} = \{w \mid uwv \in L\}$ exactly when $y$ does.
nodes.title: Syntactic equivalence via context quotients
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
